quotes.text:
- Templates are currently managed in HTML markup and we just document the ID of
  the template that the custom element expects as `Template ID: #myElementTemplate`.
  Often the template is in an include file we include anywhere the custom element
  is used.
- Styles for the custom element are usually in a separate css file with the same
  name as the module. If the element has a shadow root, the stylesheet will be
  loaded into it.

source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: The custom-element guide uses Template ID: #myElementTemplate, myElementTemplate.inc.xhtml for included markup, and my-element.css matching the module/tag family. These different spellings identify a DOM ID, include file and stylesheet. Document the required template ID, import dependent custom elements in the owning module, and load the element’s stylesheet into its shadow root when it has one. Do not convert established DOM IDs to dash spelling merely to match CSS filenames. This is a historical documented convention; the guide was retired and no global naming consistency was proved.
title: Name templates and CSS according to their different roles
